requirements.evidence: app/Models/Queue.php:24 defines DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP and :36 defaultPrefixFor (exact level first, then <=0/>=20/in-between range fallback); :58 normalizePriorityPrefixMap enforces canonical keys, one-letter A-Z values and unique effective prefixes, while the saving hook (:26-30) normalizes [] to null; :104 prefixForPriority prefers the custom map. app/Models/Ticket.php:42 nextCode scopes to queue, prefix and issue_date, skips malformed codes (:57), and app/Actions/IssueTicket.php:44-46,56-57 read the clock once for code day, issued_at and issue_date. app/Models/Ticket.php:130 casts issue_date; database/factories/TicketFactory.php:45-65 derives issue_date from issued_at and allocates the code from priority/day; app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:26,30-36,71-73 implement the optional map with ValidationException; both migrations, docs and CHANGELOG are updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes stay in app/Actions (UpdateQueue.php:28 authorizes through Gate and :30-36 validates before mutating), priority_prefix_map is deliberately absent from Queue's #[Fillable] (app/Models/Queue.php:13), and docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md plus CHANGELOG are synced with PHPDoc on the new public methods. Deviation: database/migrations/2026_10_29_042117_add_issue_date_to_tickets_table.php:39-58 provides a down() that is not reliably reversible: its grouped exists() guard compiles to SELECT * ... GROUP BY (invalid under MySQL ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY/Postgres) and it throws as soon as codes repeat across days, the normal post-launch state.

security.evidence: app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:28 authorizes before any validation or write, and :30-36 turns the model's InvalidArgumentException into ValidationException under the priority_prefix_map key; app/Models/Queue.php:13 keeps priority_prefix_map out of mass assignment; :58 rejects non-canonical keys and non-A-Z letters; app/Models/Ticket.php:57 builds its code regex only from an A-Z prefix, so user input cannot reach SQL or regex metacharacters. No new UI or Livewire surface is introduced.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/IssueTicketTest.php:22-84 cover per-priority prefixes, independent sequences, daily restarts and the single clock reading; tests/Feature/PriorityPrefixTest.php:17-162 cover defaults, custom maps, invalid keys/values/uniqueness, null normalization, UpdateQueue authorization/atomicity and the new unique index; tests/Feature/TicketFactoryTest.php:1-92 cover factory day/prefix/code behavior. No test exercises the migration backfill of existing rows from DATE(issued_at) or the down() path, so the data-migration path is unverified.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses the model normalizer in both the saving hook (app/Models/Queue.php:26-30) and UpdateQueue, keeps nextCode as one query plus a scan, and adds no service/repository layer or speculative abstraction; the default resolver is a compact const plus match.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with clear names (defaultPrefixFor, normalizePriorityPrefixMap, prefixForPriority, parseCanonicalKey), docblocks explaining the non-obvious invariants (app/Models/Ticket.php:29-46; app/Models/Queue.php:19-23,45-57), and no debug or dead code; style matches sibling models/actions.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only the queue/ticket models, IssueTicket/UpdateQueue, the two factories, the two new migrations, the related tests and the three required docs; no unrelated refactor, UI or API change.

issues.explanation: down() is effectively unusable in production: the guard throws whenever the same code exists on more than one day (the normal state after daily restarts), and its grouped exists() compiles to SELECT * ... GROUP BY, which is invalid on MySQL with ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY and on Postgres; select queue_id and code explicitly and document or handle the duplicate-data rollback path.

No test covers the migration's backfill of existing tickets from DATE(issued_at) or the down() path; the schema test only proves the final column/index shape, so a data-migration regression would go unnoticed.

review.summary: The change implements priority-based ticket code prefixes with a validated per-queue override map and per-prefix, per-day sequences, and it ships with extensive tests and synced docs. The main flow and the security/authorization requirements are met; the notable gaps are that the migration's down() is not reliably reversible on strict-SQL engines (and throws once codes repeat across days) and that the data backfill/down paths are untested.
